scope: Worksheets 10–13 and two Forces class-note pages, supplied 2026-10-04 through 2026-10-05.

sources.IMG_9427 2.HEIC: Partial duplicate of Worksheet 12; no separate additional topic
sources.IMG_9433.HEIC: Class notes: Newton laws, force inventories and third-law pairs
sources.IMG_9434.HEIC: Class notes: inertia, turning, gravitational reaction and continued motion
sources.IMG_9435.HEIC: Worksheet 13 page 1: force review, floating objects and accelerating elevators
sources.IMG_9436.HEIC: Worksheet 13 page 2: bounce, friction, buoyancy with a spring scale and loss of contact

boundaries: No friction-coefficient calculations, inclined planes, torque, pulley constraints, Hooke's law, momentum or work–energy methods are required. Spring force is supplied at one instant. Handwritten answers are reference material, not assumed correct.

questions.title: A braking laboratory shuttle
questions.source: Worksheet 10: inertia and smooth-floor motion; class notes on accelerating frames and action–reaction
questions.transfer_task: Compare two cameras during braking; combine inertia with relative displacement.
questions.distractor_models: Transmitting a brake through a frictionless deck; treating normal and weight as a third-law pair.

questions.title: A delivery robot and its winch
questions.source: Worksheet 10 conceptual: car propulsion, internal pulling, jumping; class notes on Earth recoil
questions.transfer_task: Distinguish the complete robot from its internal mechanism; identify ground traction.
questions.distractor_models: Motor treated as external; cancelling forces on different bodies; self-lifting by internal forces.

questions.title: A balance at a remote outpost
questions.source: Worksheet 10: mass versus force-defined weight, Earth/Moon, hovering
questions.transfer_task: Decode an Earth-calibrated display in a different gravitational field, then replace the source of support.
questions.distractor_models: Display mistaken for mass; Earth g used locally; gravity removed when contact is removed.

questions.title: An instrument on a workbench
questions.source: Worksheet 11: assisted support and loss of contact; Worksheet 12: mass from weight
questions.transfer_task: Infer mass from weight, decide contact status in two trials, then use the appropriate force inventory.
questions.distractor_models: N always equals mg; negative normal force; applied force mistaken for net force.

questions.title: A camera case on a stopping stage
questions.source: Worksheet 11: acceleration and scale readings; Worksheet 12: kg-calibrated scale
questions.transfer_task: Infer acceleration from downward stopping motion, predict the display, separate acceleration from velocity.
questions.distractor_models: Downward motion assumed to mean downward acceleration; changing scale reading mistaken for changing mass.

questions.title: Two instruments on a descending stage
questions.source: Worksheet 11: stacked objects in an accelerating lift
questions.transfer_task: Infer downward acceleration from observations and audit all forces on the lower object.
questions.distractor_models: Upper contact assumed to equal upper weight; upper mass omitted from floor support.

questions.title: A sensor launch
questions.source: Worksheet 10: finite-duration upward force followed by free flight; class inertia notes
questions.transfer_task: Switch force models at release and distinguish release-to-apex rise from total rise.
questions.distractor_models: Gravity omitted during contact; powered rise counted twice; force or acceleration vanishes at the apex.

questions.title: A sample container and a catching net
questions.source: Worksheet 12: stopping a falling object over a distance; Worksheet 10: upward force smaller than weight
questions.transfer_task: Infer acceleration from downward displacement, convert grams, distinguish contact force from net force.
questions.distractor_models: Omitted weight; missing factor two; any upward force assumed to slow a falling object.

questions.title: A loose vial on a turning carrier
questions.source: Class notes: turning motion, Newton's first law, force pairs and Earth's acceleration
questions.transfer_task: Predict motion in the building frame while the support turns; identify both contact and gravitational pairs.
questions.distractor_models: Constant speed confused with constant velocity; inertia treated as a force; Earth's force denied.

questions.title: Two robots separate
questions.source: Worksheet 10: internal forces and skating/jumping; class notes: Newton's third law
questions.transfer_task: Reason about two individual masses and a combined system without introducing Hooke's law.
questions.distractor_models: Equal force assumed to mean equal acceleration; internal forces called external; internal forces assumed unable to move parts.

questions.title: A specimen basket in motion
questions.source: Worksheet 12: weight-to-mass and rope-force acceleration
questions.transfer_task: Find mass, infer acceleration opposite the initial velocity, then find stopping time.
questions.distractor_models: Cable tension used as resultant; treating supported motion as free fall; newtons treated as kilograms.

questions.title: A moving test carriage
questions.source: Worksheet 12: scale calibration and inference of acceleration; Worksheet 11: apparent weight
questions.transfer_task: Use an at-rest calibration and changed force reading to reconstruct velocity, not merely the reading.
questions.distractor_models: Incorrect direction; kilogram display treated as force; display treated as changing true mass.

questions.title: A powered cart with a trailer
questions.source: Worksheet 12: two interacting blocks, inverse external-force problem
questions.transfer_task: Infer drive force from a link reading, change one subsystem's mass, predict a new link reading.
questions.distractor_models: Link force mistaken for drive force; link force assumed fixed; added mass assigned to wrong subsystem.

questions.title: Two sensors and an unknown module
questions.source: Worksheet 11: stacked-object force inventory; Worksheet 12: unknown mass from force and acceleration
questions.transfer_task: Use two independent measured contact forces to solve for an unknown mass and a signed acceleration.
questions.distractor_models: Assuming equilibrium; flipping acceleration; omitting the upper object's downward contact force.

questions.title: A motor and a magnetic brake
questions.source: Worksheet 12: opposing drive/brake forces and inferred mass; class notes: constant-velocity motion
questions.transfer_task: Infer signed acceleration from stopping time, combine opposing forces, recover mass.
questions.distractor_models: Ignoring drive during braking; adding opposing forces; omitting stopping time; motion needs continuing net force.

questions.title: An inspection capsule launcher
questions.source: Worksheet 10: powered launch then free flight; Worksheet 12: force from stopping distance
questions.transfer_task: Work backwards through free flight and powered displacement to infer the applied launch force.
questions.distractor_models: Applied force confused with ma; weight alone; powered stroke counted as free-flight rise.

questions.title: Reading a motion report
questions.source: Worksheet 10 question 2(a): motion and net force; Newton's second law
questions.transfer_task: Infer a signed net-force comparison from qualitative motion evidence and unequal masses. Variants change constant/increasing/decreasing speeds, direction, and which mass is larger.
questions.distractor_models: Faster motion needs a larger force; equal acceleration implies equal force; force always points with velocity.
questions.format: One conceptual multiple-choice part; no numerical calculation.

questions.title: Two cases make contact
questions.source: Worksheet 10 question 2(b–c): push/reaction and unequal response
questions.transfer_task: Compare a single impact interaction with the acceleration of each case, regardless of which was initially moving.
questions.distractor_models: The heavier object exerts more force; equal forces imply equal accelerations; a stationary object cannot exert a force.
questions.format: One conceptual multiple-choice part; no numerical calculation.

questions.title: Shipments from two outposts
questions.source: Worksheet 10 question 2(h–i): equal force-defined weights versus equal mass
questions.transfer_task: Use original local-gravity comparisons and either mass- or weight-matched shipments to predict response to a common force after transport.
questions.distractor_models: Equal weight implies equal mass everywhere; mass changes on transport; vertical equilibrium forbids horizontal acceleration.
questions.format: One conceptual multiple-choice part; no numerical calculation.

questions.title: Switching off a magnetic pull
questions.source: Worksheet 10 question 2(a) and 1(d): net force versus direction of motion
questions.transfer_task: Follow a changed force inventory through slowing, stopping and reversal, or continuing acceleration in the original direction.
questions.distractor_models: Zero velocity makes force disappear; motion must follow force instantly; initially balanced forces stay balanced after one is removed.
questions.format: One conceptual multiple-choice part; no numerical calculation.

questions.title: A floating sample in an accelerating elevator
questions.source: Worksheet 13 questions 4–5: floating block in an accelerating elevator
questions.transfer_task: Determine the buoyant force from the floating sample's acceleration, then reason about why the submerged fraction remains unchanged.
questions.distractor_models: Assuming equilibrium in an accelerating frame; reversing the acceleration sign; reversing buoyancy; assuming acceleration eliminates floating.

questions.title: Forces and partners on a suspended panel
questions.source: Worksheet 13 question 3 and the starred class-note quiz question on force inventories and reaction partners
questions.transfer_task: Choose one target object, list only forces acting on it, then obtain each third-law partner by reversing the two interacting object names.
questions.distractor_models: Omitting a carried load; placing another object's weight on the target diagram; pairing balancing forces; putting reaction forces on the wrong diagram.
questions.format: Two conceptual multiple-choice parts; no numerical calculation.

questions.title: A submerged artifact on a scale
questions.source: Worksheet 13 question 9: submerged block, buoyancy, spring scale and elevator acceleration
questions.transfer_task: Build the signed force equation from two upward forces and one downward force, then infer the spring-scale reading in either acceleration direction.
questions.distractor_models: Assuming equilibrium because the object is fixed in the elevator; reversing the acceleration sign; treating buoyancy as downward.

questions.title: Balancing forces versus reaction partners
questions.source: The starred class-note quiz question and Worksheet 13 question 3: forces on one object versus equal-and-opposite partners
questions.transfer_task: Use acceleration—not velocity—to compare forces on a supported case, then identify each interaction's partner on a different object.
questions.distractor_models: Assuming shared motion implies balanced forces; using velocity to infer force; treating support and weight as a third-law pair; crossing interaction partners.
questions.format: Two conceptual multiple-choice parts; no numerical calculation.
